summary: Teton lookout on Deer Creek Point, manned in 1954 and 1956, abandoned by 1970 and burned by the Forest Service in the mid-1970s; no site description found.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1960s and gone in the 1970s. The Forest Service history says the agency burned it in the mid-1970s.

access.note: The site lies on Bridger-Teton National Forest land. No source describes access to the site itself, so the level is inferred from its National Forest status.

events.note: Named in a Jackson Hole Courier item dated July 15, 1954, among Teton Forest lookouts to be manned within the next week.

Two Jackson Hole Courier items, dated August 2 and August 30, 1956. A worker went from Goosewing up to Deer Creek Lookout 'on Monday' (August 2 item) and later moved back to the ranger station 'Friday' (August 30 item). The items do not date the trips themselves. Names left out.
Forest Service history: all lookouts in the forest's southern reaches were abandoned by 1970. Firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1960s.
Forest Service history: torched or burned by the Forest Service in the mid-1970s to discourage squatters. 1975 is an approximate year.

evidence.quote: Log and frame cabin. Abandoned 1960s. Gone 1970s.

corrections.why: Firelookout.com gives the current forest as Bridger-Teton National Forest. The record's Teton National Forest matches the name used in the 1954 and 1956 items and the Forest Service history, so the older name can stay in the notes as the historical agency.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1960s. The Forest Service history says all lookouts in the southern reaches were abandoned by 1970. Both put abandonment before 1970, so the story gives the Forest Service account and the firelookout.com date.
Firelookout.com says only 'Gone 1970s'. The Forest Service history gives the cause: burned or torched by the Forest Service in the mid-1970s. The story uses the Forest Service account for the cause.

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder or design source beyond firelookout.com's 'log and frame cabin'. Do not merge this lookout with the CCC-era Deer Creek Guard Station named in the Forest Service history, which is a different building, nor with the rentable Deer Creek Cabin on Recreation.gov (a guard station near Alpine on the Greys River district). The Deer Creek name in the 1954 item and the Forest Service photo caption 'Deer Creek Lookout near Goosewing Guard Station' are taken to be the same site; the story states this as an inference, not a fact. The photo caption supports the location but gives no coordinates. The record's coordinates (43.61512, -110.19102) match firelookout.com. The 1956 items name a worker; the story omits the name. No photo added: the caption credits a USFS photo, but no image URL was retrieved. The history's abandonment and burning dates are given as 'by 1970' and 'mid-1970s'; the 1975 year on the burned event is approximate.
